lessons.title: Water and nutrient cycling in soil

scenes.say: Evaporation transfers liquid water at the surface into water vapour in the air. Cooling water vapour can condense into tiny liquid droplets in clouds. Precipitation returns water to the surface.

Nitrogen-fixing microbes convert atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia or related compounds. Some live in nodules on legume roots. Nitrifying microbes convert ammonium through nitrite to nitrate. Formation of nitrate belongs to the nitrogen cycle.

Under comparable conditions, clay usually retains more water after drainage than sand. Sandy soil often loses dissolved nutrients more readily. Crop rotation changes crop demands on soil. A fallow period can allow vegetation and soil organic matter to recover.

For JAMB, separate nitrogen fixation from nitrate formation, identify evaporation and condensation, and compare clay and sand after drainage. Blue arrows show the steps in the cycles or the movement of water.

quickCheck.prompt: What process converts atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia?
quickCheck.feedback: Nitrogen fixation makes atmospheric nitrogen available in chemically usable form.
